author: synced_reader plan, Task 8 (ReaderView + ReaderContainer, three display states)
summary: Added the player-piano ReaderView focal block and the ReaderContainer display-state escalation (embedded card -> expanded full-browser overlay -> OS fullscreen), plus a net-new useFullscreen hook wrapping the browser Fullscreen API (confirmed no existing helper anywhere in this frontend, per Task 1's findings).

changes.change: NEW — useFullscreen(elementRef): { isFullscreen, isSupported, enter, exit, toggle }. isFullscreen is derived purely from document.fullscreenElement === elementRef.current via the browser's own fullscreenchange event (never tracked independently), so a native Escape-driven exit still resolves correctly. isSupported is feature-detected (typeof elementRef.current?.requestFullscreen === 'function') and recomputed on every effect flush (no dependency array) rather than only on mount, because callers may attach the ref to a DOM node that mounts after the hook's first render (ReaderContainer's overlay only exists once displayState !== 'embedded'); a [elementRef]-keyed effect would only ever see the pre-mount null. Both isFullscreen/isSupported start at a safe default (false) rather than reading the ref during render (react-hooks/refs forbids ref reads in a useState lazy initializer).

NEW — renders the active timing group's text (segment_ids resolved via the caller-supplied segmentTextById) as the focal block, with prev/next rendered faint (opacity 0.35) for continuity. Layout: a 3-row CSS grid (1fr / auto / 2fr) puts the focal row at ~1/3 from the top regardless of container size, not margin-faked. groupProgress (0-1) continuously drives the focal block's Framer Motion animate target (translateY toward -56px, opacity toward ~0.15) so it eases upward/out as playback advances through it; AnimatePresence + a group_id key handles the actual fade-in-on-mount / fade-out-on-swap. prefers-reduced-motion (read via the existing frontend/src/hooks/useMediaQuery.ts, not a fresh matchMedia call) swaps to a plain non-animated div (data-animated="false") instead. isTrackingThisChapter===false renders an idle 'not playing' state; isTrackingThisChapter===true with activeGroup===null renders the 'sync unavailable — re-render this chapter' message (no invented estimate logic, no blank space) per 03-reader-frontend.md's no-timing-fallback section.

NEW — three-state display escalation ('embedded' | 'expanded' | 'fullscreen') driven by useFullscreen.isFullscreen (not tracked independently) plus its own displayState for the embedded<->expanded step. Design choice: the embedded card (and its expand button) stays mounted across every transition rather than being swapped out for the overlay via a mutually-exclusive branch — the overlay is position:fixed/inset:0 above it so nothing looks different, and it lets useFocusTrap's stored 'previously focused element' (the expand button) still exist in the DOM to refocus on close (a fresh remount would be a different node the stored ref could no longer focus). ReaderView renders only once at a time (inside the overlay while open; the embedded slot goes content-less and aria-hidden) so continuous groupProgress updates during playback don't double-render a hidden duplicate. role="dialog"/aria-modal="true" + useFocusTrap (frontend/src/hooks/useFocusTrap.ts, the same pattern ConfirmModal/PluginTrustModal already use) handle focus-in/focus-restore and Tab trapping. Escape closes to embedded only from 'expanded' (own keydown handler); in 'fullscreen', Escape is left to the browser's native exit, which fires fullscreenchange and is picked up by the same effect that also handles a native Esc, converging to 'expanded' not 'embedded'.

NEW — enter() calls requestFullscreen; fullscreenchange with fullscreenElement set/cleared updates isFullscreen; exit()/toggle() call document.exitFullscreen appropriately; isSupported reflects the ref'd element's requestFullscreen presence; enter() no-ops instead of throwing when unsupported.

NEW — resolves+joins segment text for the active group; idle state when not tracking; 'sync unavailable' state when tracking with activeGroup===null; data-animated toggles between the reduced-motion and Framer Motion paths based on a mocked prefers-reduced-motion match.

NEW — starts embedded; expand -> role=dialog + focus moves in; fullscreen button (mocked requestFullscreen, installed on HTMLElement.prototype before the dialog mounts, mirroring real browsers exposing the API on every element rather than one instance) -> 'fullscreen' state; a native fullscreenchange clearing fullscreenElement returns to 'expanded' not 'embedded'; Escape in 'expanded' returns to embedded and restores focus to the original expand button; fullscreen control hidden when the API is unsupported.

invariants: ReaderView/ReaderContainer never fetch or own segment text, timing data, or player-bus state themselves — they are pure presentational consumers of props Task 9's entry points will supply (activeGroup/prev/next/groupProgress/isTrackingThisChapter from useReaderSync, segmentTextById from whatever already has the chapter's segments loaded). useFullscreen's isFullscreen is only ever set from the fullscreenchange event / effect-computed snapshot, never optimistically set by enter()/exit() themselves, so it can't desync from the real DOM state.
note: Task 8 of design-docs/plans/active/synced_reader/ (04-roadmap.md), consuming Task 7's useChapterTiming/useReaderSync (read-only, not modified) per this task's scope. Task 9 (standalone reader route + Book-tab entry points + bidirectional seek) still needs to wire these components into frontend/src/app/ and frontend/src/pages/Book/. frontend/src/store/playerBus.ts and frontend/src/hooks/useChapterTiming.ts / useReaderSync.ts were explicitly not touched per this task's scope.
